newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr closes weaker in face of greenback strength.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr closes weaker in face of greenback strength.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended more than 20 basis points lower on Wednesday as the U.S. currency remained strong.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6848/55, down from 0.6871/78 at its local open. On its Trade-Weighted Index, the Kiwi was steady at 68.33 from 68.34.

Dealers noted an offshore investor had sold a reasonably large parcel of the Kiwi this afternoon, which they said was typical of U.S. players of late and probably in light of the greenback's strength.
"Kiwi slipped during the course of the day, I think on the fact that dollar/yen was 123 in the morning and ended up at 124," said a chief dealer.

"The U.S. dollar is the strongest currency in the world. If you expect Kiwi to go up in that environment then you're saying Kiwi is the strongest currency in the world -- I don't think it deserves that mantle just yet," he said.
The Australian currency was also weaker, which was adding to downward pressure on the New Zealand dollar.
However, dealers said said the Kiwi was unlikely to fall much further, one saying it may bounce off 0.6840 tonight to retest the 0.6865 area this week.
"It's still got a nice yield for many Asian deposit holders," he said.
Kiwi was seen remaining in a 0.6830-80 range for the time being.
